notes.note: Ambiguity: 'unstopped' read as any non-stopped port (started or halted); test checks queue clearing by start for both a started and a halted port.
The standard does not state the consequence of sending on a stopped port; test expects a test case error (ttcn3verdict:error), as in the operational semantics and common tool behaviour.
Uses call on a stopped procedure port; expects a test case error (consequence not stated explicitly in the clause).
Ambiguity: temporal reading chosen; test checks that a receive executed before stop has fully completed (value redirect done) after the stop.
Expects a test case error for send on a halted port (consequence not stated explicitly in the clause).
NOTE wording 'receive operations' interpreted as all receiving operations; test uses receive.
Removal of the entry behind the halt marker is not directly observable (it is unreceivable anyway); test observes removal of the entry ahead of the marker.
Hard to observe directly: test checks that after clear on a halted port, newly arriving messages cannot be received (port stays halted, marker at top).
Ambiguity: runtime reading chosen (argument passed via function parameter, case-mismatched value 'started'); compile-time case is covered by 22.05.05_test_012.
Titan accepts: it does not check constant checkstate argument values at compile time; a literal outside the allowed list violates restriction a) statically.
Titan accepts checkstate on an integer variable; this violates restriction c) (ObjectReference shall be of a port type), Titan lacks the check.
Mapped state requires map to the test system interface; executing needs a (trivial) system adapter for port sp.
